intro: Rachmaninoff recorded Chopin’s Minute Waltz for Victor in 1923, one composer-pianist playing the music of another. A long melody and an unaccompanied trill interrupt the famous circling notes.

sections.label: A · Quavers around A♭
sections.mNote: The left hand enters after the opening right-hand figure

sections.label: B · Sostenuto middle section
sections.mNote: Sostenuto: longer notes above the waltz accompaniment.

sections.label: A′ · Return of the running figure
sections.mNote: The circling figure returns, then the bass enters.

sections.label: Coda · D♭ major
sections.mNote: A final scale leads to a closing chord.

cues.title: Opening, right hand alone
cues.text: At first only the right hand plays, a quick figure circling A♭, marked leggiero. The bass then enters with a single low note followed by two chords, marking the three beats of the bar. The melody continues in running notes over this accompaniment.
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Victor recording, April 1923
cues.text: On 5 April 1923 Rachmaninoff recorded this waltz for Victor. The same day’s sessions included his recording of a piano arrangement of Strauss’s The Blue Danube.
cues.evidence: Discography of American Historical Recordings, sessions for 5 April 1923; Chopin matrix B-24192 and Strauss C-27732. https://adp.library.ucsb.edu/index.php/date/browse/1923-04-05

cues.title: Unaccompanied trill, bars 69–77
cues.text: The accompaniment stops. The right hand plays a long trill alone while the left hand rests. The running quaver figure then returns, still without accompaniment.
cues.evidence: Peters edition, bars 69–77: trill above a resting left hand, followed by the unaccompanied running figure. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=483

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: Composer for the piano, known for music that drew on operatic singing and on the irregular accents of the mazurka.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832 Chopin, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist, played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. He had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers, and teaching soon supplied his living. For the rest of his life his profession depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from one concert city to the next; Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. The family moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
